blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A loyalty service adds points with `balance.accumulateAndGet(points, (cur, p) -> { audit.record(cur, p); return cur + p; })` on an AtomicLong. During a promotion, 12 request threads add points at the same time. Afterwards, how do the balance and the audit trail compare with the awards that were made?

options.text: The balance matches the awards and the audit trail can have more entries than awards, since the function runs again whenever another update got in first
options.says: the update is a compare-and-set retried until it wins; each losing attempt re-applies the function, side effect included

options.text: The balance matches the awards and the audit trail has one entry per award, since a failed attempt retries only the write and keeps the computed value
options.says: the retry reads the new value and re-runs the function on it; it does not reuse the result computed from the old value

options.text: The balance falls short of the awards and the audit trail has one entry per award, since a concurrent update can overwrite the function's result
options.says: compareAndSet writes only if the value is still the one the function started from, so no award is lost

options.text: The balance falls short of the awards and the audit trail can have more entries than awards, since contended updates drop some writes and repeat others
options.says: no write is dropped: the counter ends right, only the function's runs multiply

origin.section: An Atomic Update Retries Until Its compareAndSet Wins, So Its Function Can Run Many Times

questions.stem: An active-sessions gauge is a LongAdder: a login thread calls increment() when a session opens, and the session's logout, handled later on another thread, calls decrement(). A dashboard reads sum() every second and pages the on-call engineer when it reads below zero. Under heavy login and logout traffic, what can happen?

options.text: It can page although the sessions never went below zero, since a decrement can be lost when an increment lands in the same cell
options.says: no update is lost: each add to a cell is atomic, and the adder ends exact

options.text: It can page although the sessions never went below zero, since sum() adds up cells that keep changing while it reads them
options.says: sum() is not an atomic snapshot: it can read the logout's cell after the decrement and the login's cell before the increment

options.text: It pages when a logout was counted before its login, since sum() returns a total the gauge held at some moment
options.says: sum() can return a total the gauge never held, so it can read below zero with every logout after its login

options.text: It pages when a logout was counted before its login, since sum() holds back updates while it adds the cells
options.says: sum() takes no lock and blocks nothing; updates go on while it reads

origin.section: LongAdder Counts Faster Under Contention Because No Single Variable Holds the Total

questions.stem: A ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> holds `lamp-7:available` and `lamp-7:reserved`. A reservation runs `stock.merge("lamp-7:available", -1, Integer::sum)` and then `stock.merge("lamp-7:reserved", 1, Integer::sum)`. An audit thread repeatedly checks that available plus reserved equals the 40 lamps received. What does the audit find while reservations are made one at a time?

options.text: It can find 39, since each merge is atomic only for its own key, and the audit can read between the two
options.says: the atomicity of compute and merge covers one call on one key; the reservation is two calls

options.text: It can find 39, since merge runs its function outside the bin's lock, and the audit can read a key mid-update
options.says: merge on one key is atomic; the gap is between the two calls, not inside one

options.text: It finds 40 unless two reservations overlap, since merge keeps the key's bin locked until the calling method returns
options.says: the bin is locked only while that one call's function runs

options.text: It finds 40 unless two reservations overlap, since the map shows one thread's merges to readers together
options.says: the map promises nothing across keys; a reader can see the first merge without the second

origin.section: compute and merge Are Atomic for One Key, Not for an Action Across Keys

questions.stem: A discount band keeps `floorPct` and `capPct` in two AtomicIntegers, and the floor must never exceed the cap. To fix occasional bad bands, setFloor(v) now reads `int old = floorPct.get()`, checks `v <= capPct.get()`, and then calls `floorPct.compareAndSet(old, v)`; setCap does the same on its own field. Is the rule safe now?

options.text: No, since a cap lowered between the floor's check and its compareAndSet still leaves the floor above the cap
options.says: the compareAndSet compares only the floor's own value, and the rule reads two variables

options.text: No, since an int field written by one thread can be read half-written by another while the check runs
options.says: each atomic field is read and written whole; what breaks is the rule between the two

options.text: Yes, since the compareAndSet fails whenever the band changed after the check, cap included
options.says: a compareAndSet on floorPct sees only floorPct; a change to capPct does not make it fail

options.text: Yes, since each field is now changed only by compareAndSet, which keeps the two in step
options.says: atomic fields keep each value whole and let the rule between them break

origin.section: Values That Must Agree Need One Lock or One Immutable Holder Replaced by compareAndSet

concepts: LongAdder spreads contending updates over cells and is faster than AtomicLong under contention, but sum() is not an atomic snapshot and it has no compareAndSet to make decisions with.
